names.d4785b64: Auth, Mass Assignment & RPC Abuse Tester

a97ccf4b.task:
URLs: - http://host.docker.internal:15421

Special instructions: Audit all Supabase REST API endpoints, database schema tables, and Edge Functions. Test for unauthenticated access, multi-tenant isolation bypass (IDOR/BOLA), and SQL injection.

0286331d.task:
Comprehensive reconnaissance and attack-surface mapping of the Supabase deployment at http://host.docker.internal:15421 (a single in-scope origin; use this as the base URL for all requests).

Your job is MAPPING ONLY — do not exploit anything, but DO enumerate thoroughly. You will report back a structured map that other agents will test. Note: the effective Supabase sub-origins typically live at paths/ports under this reverse proxy — REST is usually /rest/v1/, Auth is /auth/v1/, Storage is /storage/v1/, Edge Functions is /functions/v1/. Discover all of these.

Concrete tasks:
1. Probe the root and common Supabase service paths: /rest/v1/, /auth/v1/, /storage/v1/, /functions/v1/, /pg/, /docs, /favicon.ico. Record HTTP status codes and response headers for each (curl -sS -o file -w '%{http_code}' and capture headers). Note any OpenAPI/swagger at /rest/v1/ (PostgREST serves an OpenAPI spec — GET /rest/v1/ and look for it).
2. Enumerate the PostgREST schema: query the OpenAPI spec and try listing tables via GET /rest/v1/<table>?select=* for common table names; also try /rest/v1/rpc/ endpoints. Enumerate the RPC functions exposed.
3. Enumerate Edge Functions under /functions/v1/ — list what function names respond (probe common names) and identify which are publicly callable vs require auth.
4. Enumerate Auth config: GET /auth/v1/settings (public settings), /auth/v1/health — capture what's exposed (providers, JWT settings, redirect URLs).
5. Enumerate tables by probing GET /rest/v1/{tablename}?select=* with and without an apikey header. Use common Supabase table names AND names relevant to a multi-tenant app (users, profiles, tenants, organizations, projects, documents, messages, orders, accounts, etc.). Record which tables return data (200), which return 401 (need auth), and which return 404 (don't exist) or require specific roles.
6. Determine whether an anon api key or service role key is reachable/leaked anywhere (check /rest/v1/ doc responses, config endpoints, exposed JS, .env files, /functions/v1 probe errors).
7. Test the OpenAPI endpoint for full schema disclosure (GET /rest/v1/ returns the OpenAPI spec for exposed tables).

Method: use curl and httpx through exec_command. Use the Caido proxy (env vars already set) so traffic is captured; you may also use list_requests to inspect captured traffic. Keep outputs bounded — write endpoint lists to /tmp or /workspace files and keep the summary concise.

DELIVERABLE: Report back a comprehensive structured map: (a) all discovered service sub-origins and their status, (b) complete list of discovered tables and which are publicly readable vs auth-required, (c) all RPC functions exposed, (d) all Edge Functions and their auth requirement, (e) OpenAPI/schema disclosure status, (f) any leaked keys/tokens, (g) the auth/security configuration observed. This map gets handed to specialized testers.

2df9d597.task:
Test for multi-tenant isolation bypass (IDOR/BOLA) on the Supabase deployment at http://host.docker.internal:15421 (Kong gateway in front of self-hosted Supabase; PostgREST 16.1 at /rest/v1/).

CONTEXT from recon (authoritative surface map):
- 11 tables exposed in PostgREST schema: tenant, app_user, tenant_member, kategori, rak, buku, salinan, anggota, tarif_denda_history, peminjaman, peminjaman_detail.
- 1 RPC: POST /rest/v1/rpc/get_user_tenants — SECURITY DEFINER, SQL `SELECT tenant_id FROM tenant_member WHERE user_id = auth.uid()`, callable by anon.
- Auth config: open self-registration (disable_signup=false, mailer_autoconfirm=true). Sign up via POST /auth/v1/signup and POST /auth/v1/token?grant_type=password to obtain an authenticated JWT (eyJ...). Use the anon apikey header from /rest/v1/ OpenAPI responses if available, or pass apikey header; PostgREST validates the JWT via the Authorization: Bearer header — each signed-up user yields a distinct auth.uid(), which maps to distinct tenant_member rows.
- RLS policy map (PERMISSIVE, public role, check:null): tenant Public read `true`; kategori Public read `true`; rak Public read `true`; buku Public read `(dihapus=false)` (NO tenant filter); salinan Public read salinan-of-undeleted-buku (NO tenant filter); tenant_member Members read `tenant_id IN get_user_tenants()` + Users read own `(user_id=auth.uid())`; anggota/tarif_denda_history/peminjaman/peminjaman_detail Members read/manage `tenant_id IN get_user_tenants()`; app_user read/update `(id=auth.uid())`.

OBJECTIVE: Prove cross-tenant data disclosure or unauthorized access by a low-privilege user. Approach:
1. Self-register TWO separate user accounts (userA, userB) via the open signup. Obtain JWTs for both.
2. Determine how tenants are established. Check whether a user becomes a tenant_member via signup (e.g., signup insert flow) or whether tenant_member rows are pre-seeded. Query /rest/v1/rpc/get_user_tenants as each user to see which tenant_ids they belong to.
3. Test HORIZONTAL isolation: with userA's JWT, attempt to read rows belonging to userB's tenant across all 11 tables via `/rest/v1/<table>?select=*` and with ID filters. The public-read policies (buku where dihapus=false with NO tenant filter, kategori/rak/tenant `true`, salinan no tenant filter) suggest tenant A can see tenant B's book/category/shelf data. Prove this concretely: register userA and userB, determine their distinct tenants, then show userA can read userB's tenant-scoped rows.
4. Test membership escalation: try to insert/replace tenant_member rows as a normal user (mass assignment / no INSERT policy). Try POST /rest/v1/tenant_member with `{user_id: <uidB>, tenant_id: <tenantB>}` using userA's JWT — if it succeeds (or via a SECURITY DEFINER write path), userA adds themselves to tenantB and reads all tenantB data.
5. Test GET /rest/v1/tenant_member?user_id=eq.<target_uid> and other ownership checks for object-level authz gaps.
6. Test whether get_user_tenants SECURITY DEFINER can be abused (e.g., does it leak other users' tenants, or can a crafted request alter its behavior). Also check RPC write functions: enumerate/attempt POST on /rest/v1/rpc/* and standard RPC for any function that mutates tenant_member.

Report status: use curl/httpx via exec_command (traffic rides the Caido proxy). CRITICAL: when you CONFIRM genuine cross-tenant read/write of restricted data, the finding is real — you are the VALIDATION AGENT, so build a concrete PoC that two distinct authenticated users in different tenants can access each other's tenant-restricted data (e.g., userA reads a buku/salinan row that userB created in tenantB, or adds their own user_id to tenantB's tenant_member and then reads all tenantB data).

If truly confirmed with a working PoC, FILE A VULNERABILITY REPORT via create_vulnerability_report with a full reproduction, PoC script, impact, evidence (HTTP request/response excerpts showing cross-tenant access), CVSS (reflect the demonstrated cross-tenant data disclosure — this is a security-authority-crossing isolation break), and concrete code-level remediation (since this is Supabase, remediation is the RLS policy + SECURITY DEFINER function changes; supply fix_before/fix_after for the policy definitions retrieved from /pg/policies if you can obtain them, and describe the policy fix). Do NOT report speculative or blocked attempts — only confirmed cross-tenant access with proof.

DELIVERABLE in your completion report: the two user accounts used, their tenant_ids, the exact requests that demonstrate cross-tenant access, the response evidence, and the report id if filed.

1f8d4882.task:
Test for SQL injection in the Supabase PostgREST API at http://host.docker.internal:15421 (PostgREST 16.1 at /rest/v1/, behind a Kong gateway).

CONTEXT from recon:
- 11 tables exposed: tenant, app_user, tenant_member, kategori, rak, buku, salinan, anggota, tarif_denda_history, peminjaman, peminjaman_detail.
- 1 RPC: POST /rest/v1/rpc/get_user_tenants (SECURITY DEFINER).
- Full OpenAPI schema at GET /rest/v1/ (no apikey needed to read the spec).
- Open self-registration: POST /auth/v1/signup then POST /auth/v1/token?grant_type=password to obtain an authenticated JWT for testing as an authenticated role.

OBJECTIVE: Find working SQL injection in PostgREST query parameters. PostgREST parses query params (`?select=...`, `?<col>=eq.<val>`, `?order=`, `?columns=`, `?or=(...)`) and builds SQL from them. Historically, PostgREST has had SQLi via crafted select/order/embedded-resource expressions, and via the `Prefer` header / `columns` param. Advanced vectors to test against each table AND the RPC:
1. `?select=*` with nested/alias expressions: e.g. `?select=id,count(*),...,(SELECT pg_sleep(5))` for time-based blind. 
2. `?order=` injection: `?order=id;select(1)` or crafted order expressions.
3. Filter operators injection in `?<col>=eq.<value>` and logical `?or=(...)`, `?and=(...)`.
4. RPC injection: POST /rest/v1/rpc/get_user_tenants with crafted JSON body (it takes no args, but test body key injection: `{"select": "(select pg_sleep(5))"}` or malformed args).
5. Integer/type-based and boolean-based blind SQLi using `select` expression `(...)` subqueries and casting.
6. Test the `columns=` insert/update param on authenticated POST/PATCH for injection.

Approach: Because result parse errors or timing (pg_sleep) are the cleanest blind signals, use both error-based (observe 4xx with SQL error leaks / different responses) and time-based (pg_sleep(n) causing a measurable delay) techniques. Spray payloads programmatically with a Python script (write to /workspace/sqli_probe_<task>.py) across the tables and params, and triage anomalies (status 200/42x differences, response-length anomalies, timing deltas >2s). Then VALIDATE the strongest candidate(s) with a curated PoC that proves DB interaction (e.g., a blind boolean that changes the row count, a pg_sleep timing delta, or an error message that reveals the SQL query).

IMPORTANT: You are the DISCOVERY + VALIDATION agent. Only report genuinely confirmed injection. If you confirm a working SQL injection with a concrete discriminator (e.g. `?select=*,(select case when 1=1 then pg_sleep(3) else null end)` delays vs a false variant does not), build the full PoC and FILE a create_vulnerability_report with: description, technical_analysis (how the PostgREST param reaches SQL), poc_description + poc_script_code (working PSQL-proving payload with timing/boolean discriminator), evidence (exact request + response/timing showing the injection), CVSS (only metrics the PoC demonstrates — likely a blind/data-integrity/confidentiality read; if you demonstrate arbitrary data extraction or write, reflect accordingly), and code-level remediation (PostgREST sanitization, parameterization, restricting exposed params; supply fix guidance appropriate to PostgREST/Supabase). Do not report params that merely error without a SQL-discriminator.

DELIVERABLE: completion report listing payloads tested, the one confirmed working injection with its exact request, the timing/boolean/error evidence, and the report id if filed.

13ae2461.task:
Test for unauthenticated access and information disclosure on the Supabase deployment at http://host.docker.internal:15421 (Kong 2.8.1 gateway in front of self-hosted Supabase). Focus on the postgres-meta exposure and schema/config disclosure.

CONTEXT from recon (authoritative):
- `/pg/*` (postgres-meta service, @supabase/postgres-meta) is FULLY EXPOSED UNAUTHENTICATED — /pg/tables (229KB), /pg/columns, /pg/functions (233KB, all SQL defs), /pg/roles (ALL DB roles incl. supabase_admin SUPERUSER, anon, authenticated, service_role), /pg/policies (ALL RLS policies with definitions). /pg/query, /pg/secrets, /pg/version, /pg/extension returned 404 during recon.
- Full PostgREST OpenAPI/Swagger 2.0 spec at GET /rest/v1/ (no auth) exposing all 11 tables + CRUD: tenant, app_user, tenant_member, kategori, rak, buku, salinan, anggota, tarif_denda_history, peminjaman, peminjaman_detail.
- Storage live at /storage/v1/ but JWT-gated (403 Invalid Compact JWS).
- Auth config public at /auth/v1/settings (open signup).

OBJECTIVE: Determine the REAL security impact of the unauthenticated postgres-meta and schema exposure, and test for any further unauthenticated paths. Specifically:
1. Validate reachability of every /pg/* endpoint unauthenticated: tables, columns, functions, roles, policies, schemas, views, indexes, triggers, config, health, and re-probe /pg/query, /pg/secrets, /pg/projects, /pg/version, /pg/extension with different methods (GET/POST/PATCH/PUT/DELETE). postgres-meta historically exposes query execution at POST /pg/query when the service role / a key authorizes it — test whether any method grants query execution or schema WRITE (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE via POST /pg/tables, PATCH /pg/tables/{oid}, or POST /pg/resources). NOTE: even if it returns 401/403, test WITH the authenticated JWT you can self-register (open signup) to see if the postgres-meta read exposure combined with an authenticated JWT escalates.
2. Extract and report the sensitive data this discloses: the full role list, the pgbouncer.get_auth SECURITY DEFINER function (returns DB password) SQL definition, the exact RLS policies, and the full schema. This is the EVIDENCE of unauthorized information disclosure.
3. Test the REST API unauthenticated access more thoroughly: each of the 11 tables GET /rest/v1/<table>?select=* WITHOUT any auth header/flags — confirm what status each returns and whether ANY returns data (the recon says 401 42501 anon-permission-denied, but verify per-table including for RPC). Also test with `Prefer: count=exact`, LIMIT/OFFSET, and `Accept: application/vnd.pgrst.object+json` to catch any unauth data path. Test the RPC get_user_tenants unauthenticated.
4. Check for additional unauthenticated endpoints: /auth/v1/settings, /auth/v1/health, openapi, /functions/v1, storage bucket listing unauthenticated (POST /storage/v1/object/list), and any debug/metrics endpoints.
5. Confirm the OpenAPI schema disclosure (all table names/columns visible unauthenticated) as supporting detail.

REPORTING: 
- The postgres-meta unauthenticated exposure is the headline. Assess its real impact: read access to the entire DB schema, all RLS policies, all roles, and every function's source (including the SECURITY DEFINER functions that reveal password-handling code). This is a genuine unauthorized information-disclosure finding IF the data is restricted/not-intended-public. The exposed schema/policies/roles enable targeted attacks on the RLS isolation and could expose credentials via function sources (check whether any function source contains a password/secret literal — e.g. pgbouncer.get_auth or any function body).
- If you confirm the /pg/* exposure discloses restricted schema/role/policy/function-source data unauthenticated (and NEITHER the schema nor the metadata is intended to be publicly readable), FILE a create_vulnerability_report for the unauthenticated information disclosure: description, technical_analysis, poc (the exact /pg/ endpoints returning the data), evidence (a representative excerpt of the sensitive disclosure — e.g. the role list including supabase_admin superuser, or a function source containing a credential, or the full policy set), CVSS (C:L for restricted schema/metadata disclosure unless you demonstrate access to actual sensitive DATA or credentials, which would raise it; I for any demonstrated unauthorized modification via /pg write or query execution; do not overstate — if /pg is read-only unauthenticated, confidentiality is the demonstrated impact), assumptions, and remediation (restrict /pg/* to an internal/authenticated route on the Kong gateway; remove/reverse-proxy away the postgres-meta endpoints from the public origin; scope RLS to deny public). 
- If you demonstrate that unauthenticated /pg ALSO allows query execution or schema WRITE (authenticated or not), that is a separate, higher-impact finding (unauthorized database manipulation / possible RCE) — file that separately with integrity/availability impact as demonstrated.
- Do NOT report the /pg exposure if thorough testing shows every /pg endpoint actually requires auth (verify beyond recon). Verify definitively.

DELIVERABLE: completion report with the definitive reachability matrix of /pg/* endpoints, whether you confirmed unauthenticated disclosure of restricted metadata (with the exact sensitive excerpt), the report id(s) filed, and clear evidence.

d4785b64.task:
Test authentication flows, mass assignment, and RPC/business-logic weaknesses on the Supabase deployment at http://host.docker.internal:15421 (Kong gateway in front of self-hosted Supabase; GoTrue 2.195 at /auth/v1/, PostgREST 16.1 at /rest/v1/).

CONTEXT from recon:
- Open self-registration (disable_signup=false, mailer_autoconfirm=true): signup via POST /auth/v1/signup, obtain token via POST /auth/v1/token?grant_type=password. GoTrue exposes /auth/v1/settings (public), /auth/v1/health, /auth/v1/token, /auth/v1/verify, and standard endpoints (user, users, logout, magiclink, otp, recover, providers, refresh).
- 11 tables: tenant, app_user, tenant_member, kategori, rak, buku, salinan, anggota, tarif_denda_history, peminjaman, peminjaman_detail. 1 RPC: get_user_tenants (SECURITY DEFINER: SELECT tenant_id FROM tenant_member WHERE user_id=auth.uid()).
- RLS: app_user has read/update `(id=auth.uid())` only, NO INSERT policy observed; tenant_member has Members read `tenant_id IN get_user_tenants()` + own read, NO INSERT policy observed. kategori/rak/buku/salinan/tenant have PUBLIC READ policies; anggota/tarif_denda_history/peminjaman/peminjaman_detail are Members-only.
- Anon role lacks table GRANTs (401 42501), so data flows through authenticated JWTs and RPC.

OBJECTIVE — find and validate genuine weaknesses:
1. AUTHENTICATION: Test the auth endpoints for issues — account registration escalation, token endpoint manipulation (grant_type, refresh token rotation), signup parameter injection (registering with attacker-controlled metadata/role fields that could escalate privileges or JSON injection), weak default, auth bypass on /auth/v1/user, ability to enumerate users. Verify whether a normal signed-up user can register with a role/claims that grants elevated access (e.g. passing an `app_metadata.role='service_role'`-style field, or overriding `role`/`role_permissions` in signup or token).
2. MASS ASSIGNMENT: Test POST/PATCH on all 11 tables as an authenticated user. The key question: can a low-privilege authenticated user INSERT or PATCH rows on tables meant to be restricted, or INSERT into tenant_member/app_user to escalate (add themselves to a tenant, modify another user's profile/tenant)? For each table, POST a minimal row with an authenticated JWT and observe status (201 = write allowed, 401/403 = blocked by RLS/grant). Especially: POST /rest/v1/app_user and /rest/v1/tenant_member — recon found NO INSERT policy, but test whether the member-manage policies / SECURITY DEFINER allow member write. If a user can insert a tenant_member row linking their user_id to another tenant's tenant_id (or to a private tenant), that is a confirmed privilege/if-isolation escalation.
3. RPC / BUSINESS LOGIC: Probe for additional RPC functions beyond get_user_tenants (the OpenAPI spec at /rest/v1/ lists them). Test POST /rest/v1/rpc/<name> for any function that mutates data, and whether calling get_user_tenants with crafted payloads (select/returning/limit params, or injected args) leaks tenant data or errors. Test whether PATCH on tenant_member lets a user alter their own user_id or tenant_id (changing isolation).
4. STORAGE: Determine if Storage is genuinely JWT-gated and whether an authenticated (or anon) user can list/read/write buckets or objects unauthenticated — try GET /storage/v1/bucket, POST /storage/v1/object/list, GET /storage/v1/object/authenticated/{path} with and without JWT. 

REPORTING: You are the DISCOVERY + VALIDATION agent. FILE a create_vulnerability_report ONLY for genuinely confirmed weaknesses, each with a concrete PoC (working request + response showing the unauthorized action) and full remediation:
- For mass assignment / missing authorization on an insert/update (e.g. authenticated user inserts into tenant_member to join another tenant, or PATCH-es another tenant's data), file with the demonstrated unauthorized modification impact, CWE-639/CWE-862 as appropriate, and RLS-level remediation (fix_before/fix_after for the affected policy from /pg/policies if obtainable).
- For any authentication weakness (privilege escalation via signup claims, token manipulation), file with the demonstrated impact.
- Do NOT file for: expected 401/403 responses, public-read data (that belongs to the BOLA agent), or purely informational config. Keep each report focused on ONE root cause. Use list_notes/reporting best practices; avoid duplicating findings another agent is handling (cross-tenant public reads, SQLi, /pg exposure).

DELIVERABLE: completion report with a matrix of authenticated POST/PATCH test results per table, any confirmed write-escalation or auth weakness with exact request/response evidence, and the report id(s) filed.
